name: insert_sorted
description:
Insert value v into the sorted list xs and return a NEW sorted list
    containing all elements of xs plus v. Do not modify xs.
signature: def insert_sorted(xs: list[int], v: int) -> list[int]:
ref_impl:
def insert_sorted(xs: list[int], v: int) -> list[int]:
    out = list(xs)
    lo = 0
    while lo < len(out) and out[lo] < v:
        lo += 1
    out.insert(lo, v)
    return out

name: clamp
description:
Clamp x into the closed interval [lo, hi]: return lo if x < lo,
    hi if x > hi, otherwise x itself.
signature: def clamp(x: int, lo: int, hi: int) -> int:

name: running_max
description:
Return a list r of the same length as xs where r[i] is the maximum
    of xs[0..i] (the running maximum). xs is non-empty.
post: all(__return__[i] == max(xs[:i+1]) for i in range(len(xs)))
ref_impl:
def running_max(xs: list[int]) -> list[int]:
    out = []
    cur = xs[0]
    for v in xs:
        cur = max(cur, v)
        out.append(cur)
    return out

name: remove_duplicates
description:
Return a list with the duplicate elements of xs removed. The result
    must contain exactly the distinct elements of xs (each exactly once).

name: min_and_max
description:
Return a tuple (m, M) with the minimum and maximum element of the
    non-empty list xs.
post: all(__return__[0] <= e <= __return__[1] for e in xs)

name: count_even
description: Count how many elements of xs are even.
post: __return__ == sum(1 for e in xs if e % 2 == 0)

name: reverse_list
description:
Return a NEW list containing the elements of xs in reverse order.
    Do not modify xs.
post: all(__return__[i] == xs[len(xs) - 1 - i] for i in range(len(xs)))
ref_impl:
def reverse_list(xs: list[int]) -> list[int]:
    return list(reversed(xs))

name: merge_sorted
description:
Merge two sorted lists a and b into one sorted list containing all
    elements of both (with multiplicity).
signature: def merge_sorted(a: list[int], b: list[int]) -> list[int]:

name: index_of_value
description:
Return the index of the FIRST occurrence of v in xs. v is guaranteed
    to occur in xs.
signature: def index_of_value(xs: list[int], v: int) -> int:

name: sum_of_list
description: Return the sum of all elements of xs (0 for the empty list).

name: abs_all
description:
Return a new list where each element is the absolute value of the
    corresponding element of xs.
ref_impl:
def abs_all(xs: list[int]) -> list[int]:
    return [abs(v) for v in xs]

name: is_sorted
description: Return True iff xs is sorted in non-decreasing order.
ref_impl:
def is_sorted(xs: list[int]) -> bool:
    return all(xs[i] <= xs[i+1] for i in range(len(xs) - 1))

name: second_largest
description:
Return the second largest DISTINCT value in xs. xs is guaranteed to
    contain at least two distinct values.
post: all(e <= __return__ or e == max(xs) for e in xs)

name: split_parity
description:
Split xs into (evens, odds): a tuple of two lists, the first with all
    even elements, the second with all odd elements, each preserving the
    original relative order.

name: count_char
description:
Count the number of occurrences of character c in string s.
    c is a single character.
signature: def count_char(s: str, c: str) -> int:

name: repeat_string
description:
Return the string s repeated n times (empty string when n == 0).
    n is between 0 and 5 inclusive.
signature: def repeat_string(s: str, n: int) -> str:

name: unique_sorted
description: Return the distinct elements of xs in increasing order.
ref_impl:
def unique_sorted(xs: list[int]) -> list[int]:
    return sorted(set(xs))

name: interval_contains
description: Return True iff x lies in the closed interval [lo, hi].
signature: def interval_contains(lo: int, hi: int, x: int) -> bool:
ref_impl:
def interval_contains(lo: int, hi: int, x: int) -> bool:
    return lo <= x <= hi

name: pairwise_sums
description:
Given two lists a and b of equal length, return the element-wise sum
    list r with r[i] = a[i] + b[i].
signature: def pairwise_sums(a: list[int], b: list[int]) -> list[int]:
post: all(__return__[i] == a[i] + b[i] for i in range(len(a)))
ref_impl:
def pairwise_sums(a: list[int], b: list[int]) -> list[int]:
    return [x + y for x, y in zip(a, b)]

name: drop_smaller_than
description:
Return the elements of xs that are greater than or equal to
    threshold t, preserving order.
signature: def drop_smaller_than(xs: list[int], t: int) -> list[int]:
post: len(__return__) == sum(1 for e in xs if e >= t)
all(e in xs for e in __return__)
ref_impl:
def drop_smaller_than(xs: list[int], t: int) -> list[int]:
    return [v for v in xs if v >= t]

name: swap_ends
description:
Return a NEW list equal to xs but with the first and last elements
    swapped. xs is non-empty. Do not modify xs.
post: all(__return__[i] == xs[i] for i in range(1, len(xs) - 1))
ref_impl:
def swap_ends(xs: list[int]) -> list[int]:
    out = list(xs)
    out[0], out[-1] = out[-1], out[0]
    return out

name: rotate_left
description:
Rotate the list xs to the left by k positions and return the result
    as a NEW list. k is between 0 and len(xs) inclusive.
signature: def rotate_left(xs: list[int], k: int) -> list[int]:
post: all(__return__[i] == xs[(i + k) % len(xs)] for i in range(len(xs)))
ref_impl:
def rotate_left(xs: list[int], k: int) -> list[int]:
    return xs[k:] + xs[:k]

name: lower_bound
description:
Return the smallest index r such that all elements before r are
    strictly less than v and all elements from r on are >= v (the insertion
    point of v in the sorted list xs, before any equal elements).
signature: def lower_bound(xs: list[int], v: int) -> int:
post: all(xs[i] < v for i in range(__return__))
all(xs[i] >= v for i in range(__return__, len(xs)))

name: kth_smallest
description:
Return the k-th smallest element of xs, counting duplicates
    (1-indexed: k=1 gives the minimum).
signature: def kth_smallest(xs: list[int], k: int) -> int:
post: sum(1 for e in xs if e < __return__) < k
sum(1 for e in xs if e <= __return__) >= k
ref_impl:
def kth_smallest(xs: list[int], k: int) -> int:
    return sorted(xs)[k - 1]

name: max_subarray_sum
description:
Return the maximum sum of any non-empty contiguous subarray of the
    non-empty list xs.
post: any(__return__ == sum(xs[i:j]) for i in range(len(xs)) for j in range(i + 1, len(xs) + 1))
all(__return__ >= sum(xs[i:j]) for i in range(len(xs)) for j in range(i + 1, len(xs) + 1))

name: move_zeros
description:
Return a new list with all non-zero elements of xs first (in their
    original order) followed by all the zeros.
post: __return__ == [e for e in xs if e != 0] + [0] * xs.count(0)
ref_impl:
def move_zeros(xs: list[int]) -> list[int]:
    out = [v for v in xs if v != 0]
    out.extend([0] * xs.count(0))
    return out

name: dedupe_adjacent
description:
Collapse runs of equal adjacent elements of xs to a single element,
    preserving order (e.g. [1,1,2,1] -> [1,2,1]).
post: __return__ == [xs[i] for i in range(len(xs)) if i == 0 or xs[i] != xs[i - 1]]

name: missing_number
description:
xs contains distinct integers, each between 0 and len(xs) inclusive;
    exactly one value in that range is missing. Return the missing value.
pre: all(0 <= e <= len(xs) for e in xs)

name: running_sum
description: Return the prefix sums of xs: r[i] is the sum of xs[0..i].
post: all(__return__[i] == sum(xs[:i + 1]) for i in range(len(xs)))
ref_impl:
def running_sum(xs: list[int]) -> list[int]:
    out = []
    total = 0
    for v in xs:
        total += v
        out.append(total)
    return out

name: argmax_first
description:
Return the index of the FIRST occurrence of the maximum element of
    the non-empty list xs.
post: all(xs[i] < xs[__return__] for i in range(__return__))

name: clamp_all
description:
Clamp every element of xs into the closed interval [lo, hi] and
    return the resulting list.
signature: def clamp_all(xs: list[int], lo: int, hi: int) -> list[int]:
post: __return__ == [min(hi, max(lo, e)) for e in xs]

name: chunk_sums
description:
Split xs into consecutive chunks of size k (the last chunk may be
    shorter) and return the list of chunk sums.
signature: def chunk_sums(xs: list[int], k: int) -> list[int]:
post: all(__return__[i] == sum(xs[i * k:(i + 1) * k]) for i in range(len(__return__)))

name: repeat_each
description:
Return a list where each element of xs is repeated k times in place
    (e.g. [1,2] with k=2 -> [1,1,2,2]). k is between 0 and 4.
signature: def repeat_each(xs: list[int], k: int) -> list[int]:
post: all(__return__[i] == xs[i // k] for i in range(len(xs) * k))

name: interleave
description: Interleave two equal-length lists: return [a[0], b[0], a[1], b[1], ...].
signature: def interleave(a: list[int], b: list[int]) -> list[int]:
post: all(__return__[2 * i] == a[i] and __return__[2 * i + 1] == b[i] for i in range(len(a)))

name: two_sum_indices
description:
Return a pair of indices (i, j) with i < j such that
    xs[i] + xs[j] == target. Such a pair is guaranteed to exist.
signature: def two_sum_indices(xs: list[int], target: int) -> tuple[int, int]:
pre: any(xs[i] + xs[j] == target for i in range(len(xs)) for j in range(i + 1, len(xs)))

name: count_inversions
description: Count the pairs (i, j) with i < j and xs[i] > xs[j].
post: __return__ == sum(1 for i in range(len(xs)) for j in range(i + 1, len(xs)) if xs[i] > xs[j])

name: sum_digits
description: Return the sum of the decimal digits of the non-negative integer n.

name: int_to_binary
description:
Return the binary representation of n (0 <= n <= 1024) as a string
    of '0'/'1' characters, without leading zeros ('0' for n == 0).

name: is_anagram
description:
Return True iff strings a and b are anagrams of each other
    (same characters with the same multiplicities).
signature: def is_anagram(a: str, b: str) -> bool:

name: caesar_shift
description:
Shift every lowercase letter of s forward by k positions in the
    alphabet, wrapping around from 'z' to 'a'. s contains only lowercase
    letters a-z; 0 <= k <= 25.
signature: def caesar_shift(s: str, k: int) -> str:
pre: all('a' <= c <= 'z' for c in s)
post: all(ord(__return__[i]) == (ord(s[i]) - 97 + k) % 26 + 97 for i in range(len(s)))

name: strip_vowels
description:
Remove all vowels (a, e, i, o, u) from s and return the rest,
    preserving order.
post: __return__ == ''.join(c for c in s if c not in 'aeiou')

name: balanced_parens
description:
s consists only of '(' and ')'. Return True iff the parentheses are
    balanced: every prefix has at least as many '(' as ')', and the totals
    are equal.
pre: all(c in '()' for c in s)
post: __return__ == (s.count('(') == s.count(')') and all(s[:i + 1].count(')') <= s[:i + 1].count('(') for i in range(len(s))))

name: longest_common_prefix
description: Return the longest common prefix of strings a and b.
signature: def longest_common_prefix(a: str, b: str) -> str:
post: len(__return__) == min(len(a), len(b)) or a[len(__return__)] != b[len(__return__)]

name: sorted_squares
description:
Given a sorted list xs, return the squares of its elements in
    non-decreasing order.
post: __return__ == sorted(e * e for e in xs)
ref_impl:
def sorted_squares(xs: list[int]) -> list[int]:
    return sorted(v * v for v in xs)

name: rle_encode
description:
Run-length encode the string s: return a list of (char, count) pairs
    such that no two adjacent pairs have the same char, every count is >= 1,
    and expanding the pairs reproduces s exactly.

name: longest_run
description:
Return the length of the longest run of equal consecutive characters
    in s (0 for the empty string).
post: (len(s) == 0 and __return__ == 0) or any(i + __return__ <= len(s) and all(s[k] == s[i] for k in range(i, i + __return__)) for i in range(len(s)))
all(not (i + __return__ + 1 <= len(s) and all(s[k] == s[i] for k in range(i, i + __return__ + 1))) for i in range(len(s)))

name: first_missing_positive
description: Return the smallest positive integer (>= 1) that does not occur in xs.
post: all(k in xs for k in range(1, __return__))

name: count_pairs_with_sum
description: Count the index pairs (i, j) with i < j and xs[i] + xs[j] == t.
signature: def count_pairs_with_sum(xs: list[int], t: int) -> int:
post: __return__ == sum(1 for i in range(len(xs)) for j in range(i + 1, len(xs)) if xs[i] + xs[j] == t)

name: pivot_partition
description:
Partition xs around pivot p: return (smaller, equal, greater) where
    smaller has all elements < p, equal all elements == p, greater all
    elements > p, and together they contain exactly the elements of xs.
signature: def pivot_partition(xs: list[int], p: int) -> tuple[list[int], list[int], list[int]]:

name: mode_smallest
description:
Return the most frequent value in the non-empty list xs; break ties
    by returning the smallest such value.
post: all(xs.count(e) <= xs.count(__return__) for e in xs)
all(e >= __return__ for e in xs if xs.count(e) == xs.count(__return__))

name: add_big_digits
description:
a and b are non-negative integers represented as little-endian digit
    lists (a[0] is the least significant digit; no leading zeros except for
    the single-digit number 0). Return their sum in the same representation.
signature: def add_big_digits(a: list[int], b: list[int]) -> list[int]:
pre: all(0 <= d <= 9 for d in a)
all(0 <= d <= 9 for d in b)
post: sum(d * 10 ** i for i, d in enumerate(__return__)) == sum(d * 10 ** i for i, d in enumerate(a)) + sum(d * 10 ** i for i, d in enumerate(b))

name: sort_colors
description:
xs contains only the values 0, 1 and 2. Return the elements sorted in
    non-decreasing order (Dutch national flag).
pre: all(e in (0, 1, 2) for e in xs)

name: best_gain
description:
prices is a non-empty list. Return the maximum of prices[j] - prices[i]
    over all pairs with i <= j (0 if prices never rises).
post: __return__ == max(prices[j] - prices[i] for i in range(len(prices)) for j in range(i, len(prices)))

name: merge_intervals
description:
iv is a list of closed integer intervals (lo, hi) with lo <= hi,
    sorted by lo. Merge all overlapping or touching intervals and return the
    resulting disjoint intervals sorted by lo.
signature: def merge_intervals(iv: list[tuple[int, int]]) -> list[tuple[int, int]]:
pre: all(p[0] <= p[1] for p in iv)
all(iv[i][0] <= iv[i + 1][0] for i in range(len(iv) - 1))
post: all((any(p[0] <= x <= p[1] for p in iv)) == (any(p[0] <= x <= p[1] for p in __return__)) for x in range(-12, 13))

strategies.iv: st.lists(st.tuples(st.integers(min_value=-8, max_value=8), st.integers(min_value=0, max_value=6)), max_size=4).map(lambda ps: sorted((a, a + w) for a, w in ps))

name: gcd_bounded
description: Return the greatest common divisor of a and b (both between 1 and 60).
signature: def gcd_bounded(a: int, b: int) -> int:
post: all(a % d != 0 or b % d != 0 for d in range(__return__ + 1, min(a, b) + 1))

name: fibonacci_at
description:
Return the n-th Fibonacci number with F(0) = 0, F(1) = 1.
    n is between 0 and 15.

name: is_rotation
description:
Return True iff string b is a rotation of string a (b can be obtained
    by moving some prefix of a to its end). Every string is a rotation of
    itself; the empty string is a rotation only of the empty string.
signature: def is_rotation(a: str, b: str) -> bool:
post: __return__ == (len(a) == len(b) and (len(a) == 0 or any(a[i:] + a[:i] == b for i in range(len(a)))))

name: power_of_two_flag
description:
Return True iff n is a power of two (1, 2, 4, 8, ...).
    n is between 0 and 1024.

name: word_lengths
description:
s is a space-separated sentence with no leading/trailing spaces and no
    double spaces. Return the list of word lengths ([] is impossible: the
    empty string yields [] as specified below).
post: __return__ == ([] if s == '' else [len(w) for w in s.split(' ')])
